segments.t: What changed in the current release. The version this guide was built for is shown in the footer.

KTPH000New layoutKTPH001 — the Connection Manager shows a library on the left (all connections, favorites, recently used, open now, folders, tags, teamwork), the chosen connections in the middle and an inspector on the right, with every detail of the selected connection and quick edits of its name and tag. The toolbar uses icons in the style of the icon toolbar, and the list shows each connection's address, tag and marks for jump server, tunnels, isolation and incognito instead of emoji. See KTPH002Connection ManagerKTPH003.

KTPH000MapKTPH001 — KTPH002MapKTPH003 shows the connections as a network plan: a zone per folder in its tab color, jump-server routes and tunnels as lines, double-click connects and dragging a node into another zone moves the connection into that folder. See KTPH004List and mapKTPH005.
KTPH000FavoritesKTPH001 — mark connections with the star to find them under KTPH002FavoritesKTPH003; teamwork connections can be favorites too.
KTPH000Teamwork beside local connectionsKTPH001 — the general lists show teamwork connections too, marked with a small people symbol and read-only. See KTPH002LibraryKTPH003.

KTPH000OS symbolsKTPH001 — give each server the symbol of its operating system (Windows, macOS, Linux distributions, ChromeOS, Unix, BSD, z/OS) or one of your own images, shown in the list, on the map and in the inspector. See KTPH002OS symbolsKTPH003.
KTPH000Map as PDFKTPH001 — KTPH002PDFKTPH003 on the map saves it as a vector PDF with the korTTY logo, in landscape or portrait.

KTPH000Overview exportKTPH001 — KTPH002Export overviewKTPH003 writes your servers as JSON, YAML, TOML or XML, with the parts you choose and never a password or key. See KTPH004Exporting an overviewKTPH005.
KTPH000InspectorKTPH001 — the route from this computer through the jump server, security as chips, usage bars for the last 14 days and an SFTP button.

KTPH000Toolbar for an empty connection rowKTPH001 — while KTPH002View → Connection toolbarKTPH003 is switched on but holds no servers or groups yet, the row stays visible and offers KTPH004Add connectionKTPH005, which opens customizing on the connections catalog. See KTPH006Customizing the icon toolbarKTPH007.

KTPH000Serial portsKTPH001 — the new KTPH002SerialKTPH003 protocol opens a terminal on a serial port, like PuTTY's serial sessions: a router or switch console, a microcontroller board or a USB-to-serial adapter, on Windows, macOS and Linux. Pick the port from the list or type it, and set the speed, data bits, parity, stop bits, flow control, what Enter sends, DTR/RTS and local echo. KTPH004Send BreakKTPH005 is in the terminal's context menu and in the Connections menu, and can get a key in the keyboard settings. Serial sessions from MobaXterm and PuTTY Connection Manager files are imported too. See KTPH006Serial connectionsKTPH007.

KTPH002Clipboard protocol of kitty (OSC 5522)KTPH003 — programs that speak kitty's clipboard protocol, such as Neovim and KTPH000, can copy to the clipboard under the OSC 52 setting, and with the new KTPH004Let programs in the terminal ask to read the clipboard (OSC 5522)KTPH005 setting they can ask to read it. Every read asks you first, KTPH006DenyKTPH007 is the default, and a paste into a program that asked for paste events counts as your consent. Only text is exchanged; the strict terminal mode drops the protocol, and the policy key KTPH001 forbids reading. See KTPH008Programs reading the clipboardKTPH009.

KTPH000Scrollback memory limitKTPH001 — the new KTPH002Scrollback memoryKTPH003 slider in the Terminal settings sets the most memory the scrollback of one pane may use, from 1 to 50 MB (10 MB by default), next to the line count; whichever limit is reached first drops the oldest lines. A saved change applies to open terminals at once. See KTPH004Terminal settingsKTPH005.

KTPH000Scrollback compressionKTPH001 — while a terminal has no output, korTTY compresses the scrollback lines that are not on screen in the background, so the same memory holds several times as many lines. A line is unpacked as soon as you scroll to it. Switch it off with KTPH002Compress the scrollback in the background while idleKTPH003. See KTPH004Terminal settingsKTPH005.

KTPH000Pixel size for image tools over SSHKTPH001 — SSH sessions, isolated ones included, now tell the server the size of the terminal in pixels, so image tools that use the kitty graphics protocol size their images correctly instead of seeing 0×0.

KTPH001Disable the AI agent per connectionKTPH002 — for systems such as production servers, switch on KTPH003Disable AI agent for this connectionKTPH004 on the KTPH005AIKTPH006 tab of the connection editor. Every agent run on that connection is then refused, from the menu, the KTPH000 shortcut, accepted plans, swarm members and scheduled AI Agent jobs; KTPH007Ask AgentKTPH008, KTPH009AI PlanningKTPH010 and the other AI features stay available. See KTPH011Connections without the agentKTPH012.
KTPH000Search the connection skillsKTPH001 — a search field above the AI Skills list in the connection editor filters them by name, description and tags.

KTPH000Snippet Manager windows no longer block the main windowKTPH001 — the terminals stay usable while a Snippet Manager window is open, also while it asks a question or runs a Full code analysis. KTPH002Tools → New Snippet Manager WindowKTPH003 opens a further one, and KTPH004Move to new windowKTPH005 on a tab moves a snippet or a folder analysis into a window of its own, for example on a second screen. See KTPH006Opening the Snippet ManagerKTPH007.

KTPH001Cline and Antigravity CLIKTPH002 — the Coding Agents panel now recognises KTPH003ClineKTPH004 and Google's KTPH005Antigravity CLIKTPH006 (KTPH000), the successor to Gemini CLI; the rules of every other agent were re-checked against its latest version, and Gemini CLI's folder-trust and sign-in dialogs now count as waiting for you. See KTPH007What it detectsKTPH008.

KTPH008Copying from the AI chatKTPH009 — KTPH010KTPH000KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH001KTPH013 / KTPH014KTPH002KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH003KTPH017 and KTPH018KTPH004KTPH019+KTPH020KTPH005KTPH021 / KTPH022KTPH006KTPH023+KTPH024KTPH007KTPH025 now work after clicking into a chat message, and the chat's scrollbar is wider and easier to see.

KTPH000Wide dialogs open at their size in the AtlantaFX designsKTPH001 — under an AtlantaFX design, a dialog laid out wider than 600 px (such as the settings, KTPH002Compare foldersKTPH003 in the SFTP manager or the KTPH004Logfile ManagerKTPH005) opened squeezed or grew after it appeared; it now opens as wide as in the Normal design, and a long message still wraps.
